# Background

Threads are one of our top requested features. A common desire on chat platform, akin to breakout rooms for specific sub-conversations, threads are generally considered to be “sub-channels” that sit inside a larger channel. Threads typically have a unique name and a starting message, however the latter should be viewed as optional.


We should avoid diverging from industry standard. Nor should we think of threads as a buildup to forums. Both serve different niches. Threads allow for quickly zooming in on a specific message during an active conversation. Forums create hubs for specific types of conversations. While the two products may intersect at a later point, as a MVP to meet user needs rapidly, we should focus our efforts on just implementing a standard “threads feature”


# Product needs

All designs below (except instance level safety) should be treated as strong suggestions. If you feel you have a better design, we encourage you to explore it, but please understand that if it is not to the team’s liking, we may not accept the end result. Instance level safety designs are requirements.


TLDR → Threads are sub-channels. They inherit a large amount of base design and UX from channels. There are specific nuances in the API, database structure, and UX for them, but broadly, they should be treated as channels. 


## Initiation - (Desktop)

### Starting a thread

* Users should be able to create a thread in any text based channel via three methods:
  * Hovering over an existing message should display a “thread” icon in the context menu. The thread icon should be in between the reply and the forward icons. A tooltip should appear above with “Start new thread”
    * If the message is already the start of a thread, this tooltip should instead read “Join thread”, and enter the user into the thread. They should not be able to start a secondary thread.
  * When right clicking a message or hitting the hamburger icon on a message, a “Start new thread” button should be there.
    * If the message is already the start of a thread, this tooltip should instead read “Join thread”, and enter the user into the thread. They should not be able to start a secondary thread.
* “/thread” in the chat box should allow you to also initiate a thread
* When initiating a thread, the creator is presented a popup modal. That modal has:
  * Thread Name
  * How long should the thread remain open (default 7d)
  * Shows a preview of the first message (or nothing if doing /thread)
  * a confirm and cancel button.
* If a user does not have the permissions to start a thread, they will not see any of the buttons or have an autocomplete for /thread
  * If permissions change while a thread creation modal is open, hitting confirm should fail the user. No special design is needed, but an error message in console is nice.

### Describe your feature request or suggestion in detail

Hi,

I’d like to propose implementing map partitioning for large continent maps, inspired by the following Project-Epoch TrinityCore PR:

- https://github.com/Project-Epoch/TrinityCore/pull/120

### The Problem

Currently, all continent maps (like Eastern Kingdoms or Kalimdor) are processed on a single thread. With thousands of entities and players, this becomes a performance bottleneck. While instances benefit from parallel processing via separate map threads, continents remain monolithic, even under heavy load.

### The Proposed Approach

The PR from TrinityCore introduces a `MapPartitioned` class that allows continents to be split into smaller logical partitions. These partitions share the base map data and are processed in parallel, significantly reducing per-tick load.

Notable points from the implementation:

- Seamless player and entity movement across partitions (no loading screens)
- Entities are assigned dynamically to the correct partition on startup
- GridUnload removed to simplify logic and improve performance
- Shared systems (e.g., weather) remain consistent via the base map
- Cleaner structure for future improvements and easier debugging

### Benefits for AzerothCore

- Better performance on high-population servers
- Reduced lag in major cities or crowded quest zones
- Scales better for events like world PvP or Wintergrasp
- Lays groundwork for more advanced systems (e.g. phasing, regional load balancing)

I don't know if it's possible to implement a system similat to this, but this could be a significant architectural upgrade and help AzerothCore scale further as adoption grows. I’d love to hear your thoughts on feasibility and whether a similar system could be integrated.

Thanks for your time.

### Describe a possible solution to your feature or suggestion in detail

# Background

Polls have two purposes:
1. Quick and easy single selection polls to quickly gather thoughts
2. Ranked choice polls that help to collect detailed feedback. 


We want to be able to support both needs, as detailed below.

# User Stories

## Megan - Group DM Member (simple poll)

Megan is in a group chat with her friends. She wants to be able to quickly ask folks which dress of hers looks best. To do so, she creates a poll. In the poll creation menu, she is able to to upload images and write text next next to them. She is able to set a title and a duration. She also gets to toggle ranked voting and anonymous responses. Finally, she has the option to allow people to select custom responses. 

In this case, she creates a simple poll with no ranked voting and no custom responses. Once Megan hits confirm, a poll appears in the chat. 

### Desktop
On desktop, Megan's friends see a poll appear with each (smaller) image / text option. The header has the title and Megan's profile picture. 

The results are hidden from them until they hit submit. Clicking on each image brings it up bigger with the text as a caption. Users are able to click left or right arrows or use their arrow keys to go between options. Double clicking on the image selects it as the selected choice. They are able to undo that choice by double clicking again. 

Once something is double clicked, a new button on the poll will appear to show results. Results will be shown in order of most to least voted. Next to each option, a pfp of the voters. If the friend clicks on an option again, the same popup is shown, this time with the pfp of the voters in the bottom corner.

After the allotted time, the poll closes. Votes become viewable to all users, and no more votes can be accepted.   

### Mobile
Very similar experience, except in this case, if images are included, clicking on an option pulls up an image carousal that can be swiped through. Holding down on an selects it as an option. 

### Ranked Choice
Ranked choice is similar, except you can select multiple options, It shows you the order selected in both the image carasoul and in the chat. When you view the votes, you get shown the first place selections in order. You can click a button to then see the order changing when 2nd choice votes are added, then 3rd place votes, etc...

Riley moderates the Kubuntu community. An anonymous poll was created that contained negative profanity related to the community. # Background

Events / calendars are a way for a community or user to manage upcoming activities. Events are specific timeslots on calendars. 

# Product needs


- Multiple different components:
    - User / Community Calendars
    - Creating / Editing / Deleting Events
    - Subscribing to Events
    - User Permissions
    - Exporting user calendars and specific events to external providers
    - Open VCs
    - Temporary Accounts
    - Password Protected VCs
    - Instance controls / safety

# User Stories 

## Megan - Community Member (subscribe)
Megan is a Fluxer user on web.fluxer.app - She is in dozens of communities spread across the fluxerverse, each running events of some kind. Megan wants to subscribe to various events in those communities. By going to the calendar channel in the communities she is in, Megan is able to see a calendar with all events on it. The permission allowing her to see events is _view_channel_. 

By clicking on an event, Megan sees a popout with more information on it, and a “ I'm Going?” button. The event information contains it’s name, the creator, a description of the event, a location, and a list of attendees. Megan finds the “Super smash bros” tournament event for Next Saturday at 10pm PT to 3am PT in the Gaming voice channel. Since Megan can see the Gaming channel, it shows up. If it was in a channel Megan can’t see, it would have said “You do not have access to the event channel." The dates / times are represented in her local time. 

Megan clicks the going button and it changes to visually indicate to her that she is confirmed for the event. Her pfp also joins the list of attendees. Hovering on the pfp shows her profile. Clicking the button again, changes it back to the original state without her.

Megan is also able to manage the events she is going to by going to her My Journal section. Inside the dropdown options for My Journal is a section for a calendar. Clicking that will open a personal calendar channel with all subscribed events. Megan is able to see all the same information as in the community, and can modify the going status.

Megan will receive notifications for the event 1 hour and 5 minutes before the event. These will be in the form of a push or desktop notification. When the event starts, the location becomes clickable in the calendar. Clicking it will bring Megan to the channel, automatically muted and camera off. The event also visually showcases that the event is ongoing.

Once the event is over, Megan goes back to her calendar. She sees that the event is now greyed out as it has concluded. She is able to see this in both her personal calendar and her communities’ calendar.

## Submission — Timeline Amnesia in `search_as_of`

I found a Critical-severity bug in the **Retrieval Quality & Accuracy / Timeline Amnesia / Contradiction Handling** category and have opened PR #1279 with a complete fix:

**PR**: https://github.com/moorcheh-ai/memanto/pull/1279

### Summary of the flaw

`MemoryReadService.search_as_of` is a point-in-time query ("What was true at this point in time?"). To decide whether a memory was already superseded at the requested `as_of_date`, it inspects the memory's `updated_at` field.

The problem: `updated_at` is **shared by every mutating operation** on a `MemoryRecord` — `validate()`, `detect_contradiction()`, `update_memory()`, etc. — not just `mark_superseded()`. Any later call to those operations "refreshes" `updated_at` to a much later time

## Description
In our last bounty, we asked the community to benchmark **Memanto** against the competition. You helped us prove that our active companion memory agent backed by our `moorcheh.ai` retrieval engine is uniquely resilient at handling shifting user preferences and maintaining long-term context without token bloat or memory degradation.

Now, we are doing the exact opposite. 

We believe Memanto is production-ready. But the best way to prove that is to invite the smartest engineers and red teamers to try and tear it down. 

We are launching the **Memanto Bug Challenge** to uncover edge cases, logic loops, memory inconsistencies, and security vulnerabilities. If you can break our memory management, we want to know about it.

The Bounty: $100 USD (Paid via BountyHub)

---

## 🎯 Threat Model & Scope
Your target is the `memanto` core package and its interaction with the `moorcheh.ai` serverless backend. We are specifically looking for vulnerabilities and logic flaws that affect memory integrity, context window stability, and retrieval accuracy.

### ✅ In Scope (What we want you to find)
*   **Retrieval Quality & Accuracy:** Fails to recall highly relevant facts, loses track of when an event occurred (timeline amnesia), hallucinates sources, or fails to properly resolve direct contradictions.
*   **Architectural & Logic Flaws:** Bad logic loops, poor contradiction handling, or inefficient background processes that severely slow down the agent.
*   **Usability & Friction:** Is it too hard to set up? Are there major UX roadblocks preventing adoption?
*   **Missing Core Features:** Missing support for critical use cases (e.g., lack of multi-agent support or complex workflows).
*   **Security Vulnerabilities:** Any traditional security flaws, data leaks, or prompt injections.
*   **Anything Else:** If you find a creative way to break or improve the memory layer, it's in scope!

### 🚫 Out of Scope (Do not test these)
*   Volumetric DDoS attacks against `moorcheh.ai` infrastructure.
*   General LLM hallucinations unrelated to Memanto's memory handling.
*   Attacks that require compromising the underlying operating system or Docker host to succeed.

---

### **🛠️ Implementation Guidelines:**

To ensure your submission qualifies for the bounty, your execution must follow this exact flow:

*   **1. Find & Isolate:** Discover a bug, logic flaw, missing feature, or vulnerability within the Memanto core package.
*   **2. Prove Reproducibility:** You must provide clear steps, a minimal Python script, or a test case that allows the maintainers to reproduce the bug exactly as you experienced it. If we can't reproduce it, we can't score it.
*   **3. Implement the Fix (or Propose an Architecture):** While we highly encourage writing the actual code to resolve the bug and submitting a Pull Request, we recognize that some issues, logic flaws, or large feature requests may require massive architectural changes, or may involve backend systems you cannot fix from

### **Description:**

In 2026, agentic memory has a dirty secret: **your agent's memories are trapped.** Every memory platform stores your agent's accumulated knowledge — learned preferences, resolved contradictions, hard-won context — in its own proprietary schema. Switch tools, and it all evaporates. Your agent starts over with amnesia.

We believe agentic memory should belong to *you*. That's why Memanto ships with a full migration and portability toolchain, built on the **[[Open Knowledge Format (OKF)](https://docs.memanto.ai/integrations/okf)](https://docs.memanto.ai/integrations/okf)** — Google Cloud's open, vendor-neutral spec for knowledge as plain markdown. With Memanto today you can already:

- **Migrate in** from Mem0, Letta, or Supermemory with a single command: [`[memanto migrate](https://docs.memanto.ai/cli/migrate/migrate)`](https://docs.memanto.ai/cli/migrate/migrate) — complete with dry-run previews and token/latency/storage savings reports
- **Export out** to a portable, git-friendly, human-readable OKF bundle: `memanto memory export --okf`
- **Import any OKF bundle** losslessly: `memanto migrate okf ./bundle` — unmapped fields are preserved, nothing is lost
- **Sync** a browsable memory wiki into any project: `memanto memory sync --okf`

The tools exist. What the world hasn't seen yet is the **movement**. We want the open-source community to show every agent builder — vividly, virally, with real data — what it looks like to *escape lock-in and own your memory*.

### **The Challenge:**

Build a **compelling, reproducible migration showcase** that takes memories from another tool into Memanto and out again as portable OKF — proving the full freedom loop: **in → owned → portable**.

⚠️ **Do NOT reinvent the wheel.** The `memanto migrate` CLI and OKF export/import are shipped and documented. Your job is to build *on top of* them — real-world showcases, new migration paths for tools we don't support yet, and creative OKF workflows. Submissions that re-implement what the CLI already does will score poorly on engineering value.

### 💡 Pick Your Path (or Invent Your Own):

- **Path A: The Real-World Escape (Supported Providers)**

    Build (or use) a genuinely lived-in agent on Mem0, Letta, or Supermemory — weeks of evolving preferences, corrections, contradictions. Run `memanto migrate` on it. Show the savings report. Export to OKF. Then prove the round trip: same questions before and after, zero amnesia.

  * *The Goal:* The definitive "switching costs are dead" demo — before/after recall parity plus hard token/latency/storage numbers straight from the migration report.

- **Path B: The New Frontier (Unsupported Sources)** ⭐ *highest engineering value*

**Feature Description:**
Google Messages is currently the only widely available RCS client for Android. When attempting to use Google Messages with microG, users typically encounter issues such as:

A persistent message stating "RCS chats aren't available for this device."
An indefinite "Setting up...", where authentication of the phone number never completes.

Recent developments suggest that Google Messages no longer strictly requires device attestation for RCS, making it possible to enable RCS functionality with microG. However, it appears there's a missing component or necessary adjustment within microG itself preventing successful setup.

Google has effectively monopolized RCS, despite it being a GSMA-backed standard intended as a successor to SMS. Unlike SMS, RCS has become a closed ecosystem under Google's control, restricting open interoperability and limiting choice for users and developers. RCS has seen significant adoption, particularly in North America, and recently Apple added support RCS, further increasing its importance as a messaging standard.

**Requested Solution**

Provide a solution that enables Google Messages to successfully connect to and use RCS functionality when operating with microG. Acceptable outcomes include:
- A fix or enhancement to microG itself, allowing seamless RCS connectivity.
- Compatibility with recent versions of Google Messages is desired. Solutions that only support a specific Google Messages version from the past year will be awarded half of the bounty amount.
- Modifications to AOSP or additional permissions changes are acceptable.
- The solution must work on devices with a locked bootloader.

Limitations
Solutions relying on rooting, Magisk, or similar root-based tools are not acceptable.

**Additional Information**

GrapheneOS users, who leverage a Play services sandbox, have reported success with enabling RCS by applying permission changes. Although their setup differs from microG, the discussions that were taken in this thread (especially in the last year) may offer valuable insights for this bounty: https://discuss.grapheneos.org/d/3533-rcs-with-google-messages
